PRIOR RESEARCH — OSS practice for programmatic git (commissioned 2026-07-31 for bug 747f; recorded
here because 747f is closed and this is the live ticket for the class).

NOTE: this ticket also carries junk comments whose body is the literal text "--body". Those are mine:
`rebar comment` takes a POSITIONAL body (`rebar comment <id> <body>`), not a `--body` flag, so the
text was discarded. This comment is the re-write. Ignore the "--body" entries.

== 1. Git batches missing-blob fetches ONLY via unpack-trees ==
Documentation/technical/partial-clone: "checkout (and any other command using unpack-trees) has been
taught to bulk pre-fetch all required missing blobs in a single batch." Confirmed in source:
unpack-trees.c calls prefetch_cache_entries() inside check_updates(), gated on
repo_has_promisor_remote(); check_updates() runs ONLY when the working tree is updated.
builtin/checkout-index.c contains NO prefetch at all. So `read-tree <sha>` (no -u) + `checkout-index
--all` is exactly the path git never taught to batch. That was 747f's real mechanism, NOT the filter alone.
  https://git-scm.com/docs/partial-clone
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/git/git/master/unpack-trees.c
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/git/git/master/builtin/checkout-index.c

== 2. Ecosystem rule: FILTER IFF YOU WILL NOT MATERIALIZE ==
actions/checkout is the reference implementation (src/git-source-provider.ts): blob:none is applied
ONLY on explicit request, or when sparseCheckout means most blobs are never materialized. The default
full checkout is never filtered. No mature tool was found that filters a ref it will check out in
full and relies on lazy fetch.
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/actions/checkout/main/src/git-source-provider.ts

== 3. Batched refill options, strongest first ==
- Do not filter the ref you materialize (one RPC, server-side delta compression). Oldest, fully supported.
- Route through unpack-trees (read-tree -u) so git batches for you. SOURCE-READING, NOT cited
  practice — reproduce before relying on it.
- git backfill (>= 2.49, EXPERIMENTAL): https://git-scm.com/docs/git-backfill
- `git rev-list --objects --missing=print` -> batched fetch. The idiom git's own design doc names.
- `git fetch --refetch` reapplies a changed filter but refetches EVERYTHING — wrong granularity.
- `git cat-file --batch` as promisor prefetch: NO evidence it batches. Do not build on it.

== 4. Do not latch promisor state onto a repo the tool does not own ==
Every mature tool examined does partial/shallow work in storage IT owns: cargo (~/.cargo/git/db, and
it uses shallow not blobless), gclient/depot_tools (dedicated cache_dir), actions/checkout (throwaway
CI workspace), Scalar (creates the blobless clone itself). EVIDENCE CAVEAT: this is a UNIFORM ABSENCE
of counterexamples, not a written prohibition — a weaker evidence class, reported as such. Known
failure mode: once remote.origin.promisor + partialclonefilter latch, changing the remote breaks
pushes (desktop/desktop#16284). Established mitigations: separate clone/cache dir,
GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_INDEX_FILE isolation, --no-write-fetch-head.

== 5. TIMEOUTS ON PROGRAMMATIC GIT: NO SETTLED PRACTICE (flagged as genuinely unsettled) ==
Git has no --timeout on fetch. actions/checkout — the most-executed git automation in the ecosystem —
ships NO timeout on any git subprocess and relies on the CI job timeout. Practice splits between an
outer-process timeout (Python subprocess timeout=) and git-native transport bounds, which are more
precise and UNDERUSED:
  http.lowSpeedLimit / http.lowSpeedTime — "If the HTTP transfer speed ... is less than
  http.lowSpeedLimit for longer than http.lowSpeedTime seconds, the transfer is aborted."
  Overridable via GIT_HTTP_LOW_SPEED_LIMIT / GIT_HTTP_LOW_SPEED_TIME. Plus
  GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh -o ConnectTimeout=..." for SSH.
They COMPOSE: a subprocess timeout bounds total wall time; http.lowSpeed* kills a stalled connection
in seconds rather than burning the whole budget.
>>> DIRECTLY RELEVANT HERE AND TO 983f: rebar uses ONLY the outer-process form (_GIT_TIMEOUT) and
sets NO git-native transport bound anywhere. Consider that gap as part of this ticket.

== 6. GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH — version floor corrected, and it CANNOT be a guard ==
Documented/user-facing from commit e6d5479 (2024-02-27), shipping in git 2.45.0 — NOT 2.43 as bug
747f's text claimed. Git silently ignores env vars it does not know, so on git < 2.45 it FAILS OPEN
with no signal — useless as a production guard on exactly the old-git environments where you would
most want one. Legitimate use is as a TEST ASSERTION (the docs position it alongside `git cat-file
-e` as a probe). 747f shipped it that way.
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/git/git/master/Documentation/git.adoc

== Explicitly flagged as having NO settled ecosystem practice ==
- Timeouts on programmatic git network calls (see 5).
- Whether a tool may convert a repo it does not own into a partial clone (see 4 — uniform absence only).
- git backfill semantics (documented as subject to change).
- git cat-file --batch as a promisor prefetch mechanism (unverified).
